plan.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
plan.story:
Maya tossed a tennis ball straight up for a serve. It seemed to hang above her. She swung and missed.

"I thought it was waiting up there," she said.

She tossed it again and watched. The ball rose more slowly, stopped for an instant at the top, and then started down.

"If it stopped, why did it come back down?"

At the top of the throw, the ball had stopped moving upward. For that instant its velocity was zero. But nothing was holding it up.

Gravity was still pulling down. It had slowed the ball on the way up, and now it was speeding it up on the way down.

On her next toss, Maya started her swing a little earlier. This time she heard the ball pop against the strings.
plan.cardDescription: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant. Gravity is already pulling it downward.
plan.learningGoal: Say that gravity still pulls the ball down at the top of its throw, where it is still for an instant.
plan.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows. Press Play again to watch the ball fall, or drag the timeline to inspect any moment.

scene.description: One moving ball on a fixed height scale with a launch-height guide; the scale does not change with the launch speed, so a faster toss visibly rises higher. A blue Motion arrow beside the ball shortens on the way up, is absent at the top and points down on the way back. A separate dashed warm gravity arrow keeps the same direction and length throughout. Beside the ball a callout (frame object id callout.toss) reads Moving up, Still for an instant or Moving down, with Gravity pulls down always shown. The scene starts at launch and runs the whole rise and fall. No second ball, graph, equation, number readout or comparison strip.

The gravity arrow keeps the same direction and length, so gravity pulls down at the top too.
A faster toss reaches its top later and higher on the same fixed height scale.

controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time since launch
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: See how the speed of the toss moves the top without changing what gravity does there.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the pull does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: At top
controls.purpose: Jump to the top of the toss and pause there.
controls.selectionReason: The top is the one instant the explanation is about; a button reaches it exactly, which dragging the scrubber does not.
controls.effect: Seeks the top marker and pauses.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.selectionReason: Replay keeps the settings; Reset restores them so the learner can start over.
controls.effect: Restores launch speed 4.0 m/s, time 0 and paused.

assumptions: Gravity fixed at 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.

claims.text: At the top the velocity is zero and the acceleration is still 9.8 m/s^2 downward, so gravity keeps pulling.
claims.check: Differentiate v = u - g t: the slope is -g at every t, including the top.
